Since he was being conquered by the blows from above, he was already flowing towards unwillingness, with his whole land being in danger, and then he was devising various ways of hindrance for them, and not completely lifting the yoke of slavery, he was trying to hinder them in another way, saying they should go and sacrifice to the Lord their God in his land. For what did he say to Pharaoh, 'Go, sacrifice to the Lord your God in my land?' for it is not possible to be thus; for no one can serve two masters; and there is a weakness of the uninitiated and a creation of those who are being perfected in virtue, and to those who are so divided, to give equal diligence, so that the mind that is diseased may be softened, but again strengthened to what is pleasing to God, calling the accusation most just; through which things he knew to honor, what was necessary to choose and only, how would he not strongly accuse their shamefulness? Then how would he himself proclaim the scripture, being a wicked worker, having been condemned? Therefore, we need a noble and youthful mindset to be able to go well to God through all good work, completely and entirely; which will be possible for us, and very easily, if we wish to follow the ancient types; therefore, we see the Israelites, having to throw off that most dishonorable slavery, and to overcome the hand of those who formerly prevailed, and not to do any of those things, unless they had sacrificed the lamb in Egypt as a type of Christ, and had been anointed with the blood, and had eaten unleavened bread on it; therefore, our souls must be fortified through the truest and most mystical blessing, if we renounce serving sins.

For one could not otherwise escape the irresistible down-rushes from earthly passions, unless through participation in Christ to weaken the power of Pharaoh, that is, of Satan. For this reason, although being God by nature and having been declared the Only-Begotten of God the Father, He voluntarily came down to emptiness, taking the form of a servant, as it is written, and being found in the likeness of a man, so that He might elevate the lowliness of our nature to great heights, granting it its own security. For being unchangeable by nature and unable to suffer, He inseparably mingled Himself with human nature, which is easily inclined towards all kinds of evil. As I said recently, He gave the security of His own nature to ours, which is weak, so that our mind might be firmly established in good works, and the passions of the flesh might be completely mortified by the power of the indwelling God, the Word. And so Paul sends a message saying…

For the law's inability, in which it was weak through the flesh, God sent his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and condemned sin in the flesh, so that the law's requirement might be fulfilled in us who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. Therefore, sin has been condemned, having been put to death first in Christ and to be put to death also in us when we dwell in him with our own souls through faith and the participation of the Spirit, making us conformed to Christ through the quality of holiness. For the Spirit of our Savior Christ is a certain form of him, somehow bearing our divine image through himself. Thus, the Spirit is not different from Christ, as far as the identity of substance and divine energy are concerned. When our Savior says, 'I am the truth,' John writes that 'the Spirit is the truth,' and Paul, who was nurtured on the sacred Scriptures, says, 'The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.' You hear how the mystagogue has preserved the unity of the Son and the Holy Spirit, both in substance and in distinct conception, according to what is said to exist, which each is said to be and truly is.

For the Spirit is reasonably considered to be the Spirit, and not the Son, but rather the Spirit of the Son, forming and transforming into itself the things in which it participates, so that God and the Father, seeing the characters of his own offspring in us, may love us as children and honor us with heavenly honors. This would be a clear demonstration of the ancient decree through the all-wise Moses. For what did he say? 'Sanctify to me every firstborn, every firstborn that opens the womb.' By saying 'Sanctify', he meant 'Register and dedicate as holy and indebted to God'. For it seems that Moses was not considered to be a mere servant, but rather a minister of the divine and holy Spirit, and the one who was entrusted with the master's privileges, and was able to accomplish the things that are proper to God alone. What then did Moses mean? What did he say to the sons of Israel? pass_b_english: To achieve purification from earthly impurities, it is necessary to escape the grasp of those who have taken advantage of us, so that we might approach the services to God in purity, being pure and acting purely.
The great Moses was calling the Israelites to do this when he led them to the pure desert, away from the corrupting influences of Egypt.
However, Pharaoh was puffed up and trampled on the divine glory, refusing to acknowledge the Lord and insisting that he would not let the Israelites go.
As Pharaoh was being conquered by the blows from above, he became increasingly unwilling to let the Israelites go, and his whole land was in danger, ultimately leading to his downfall.

In his attempts to hinder the Israelites, Pharaoh devised various ways to keep them in slavery, saying that they could go and sacrifice to the Lord their God in his land, but this was just another ploy to keep them under his control and prevent them from truly serving God.
We see how even when the law of God leads us out of sin, Satan rises up in opposition.
Our Savior Jesus Christ, who has surpassed all life, is involuntarily dragging away greed, not having a field for a cavalry.
But he does not allow us to be completely outside of our own land; instead, we are to share, as he commands, both in what seems good to him and in what is pleasing to the Master of all.

Ultimately, it is impossible for us to have a blameless way of service unless we have completely gone out of the devil's land and are found to be completely without a share in his slavery, having been set free by Christ.
Moses said to Pharaoh, 'Go, sacrifice to the Lord your God in my land,' which implies that it is not possible to serve two masters.
This is because no one can simultaneously fulfill the demands of two conflicting authorities, and we must choose to serve either God or the devil.
The Israelites, having been enslaved in Egypt, had to throw off the yoke of their oppressors and overcome the hand of those who formerly prevailed, trusting in God's power to deliver them.

They were able to do so because they had sacrificed the lamb in Egypt as a type of Christ, and had been anointed with the blood, and had eaten unleavened bread on it, foreshadowing the redemption that would come through Christ.
Our souls must be fortified through the truest and most mystical blessing, if we renounce serving sins and instead choose to follow God's will.
The only way to escape the overwhelming power of earthly passions is through our participation in Christ, which enables us to weaken the power of Satan.
This is why Christ, who is God by nature and the Only-Begotten of God the Father, voluntarily came down to emptiness, taking on the form of a servant.
He did this to elevate the lowliness of our human nature to great heights, granting it the security that it lacks.

By mingling Himself with our nature, which is prone to evil, Christ gave us the security of His own unchangeable nature, so that our minds might be firmly established in good works and our flesh might be transformed.
As a result, the passions of our flesh are completely mortified by the power of the indwelling God, the Word.
Paul conveys to us a message of hope and transformation through our participation in Christ.

God sent his own Son in a body like ours, prone to sin, and condemned sin in that body, so that the law's demands might be fully met in us who do not live according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

As a result, sin has been condemned and put to death, first in Christ and eventually in us, when we allow him to dwell in our hearts through faith and the Spirit's presence, transforming us into his likeness through the power of holiness.
The Spirit of our Savior Christ is, in a sense, a reflection of him, bearing the image of our divine nature.
Jesus said, 'I am the truth' (John 14:6), and John wrote, 'The Spirit is the truth' (1 John 5:6).
Paul said, 'The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom' (2 Corinthians 3:17).
The mystagogue has preserved the unity of the Son and the Holy Spirit, both in substance and in distinct conception, according to what is said to exist, which each is said to be and truly is.

The Spirit is reasonably considered to be the Spirit, and not the Son, but rather the Spirit of the Son, forming and transforming into itself the things in which it participates, so that God and the Father, seeing the characters of his own offspring in us, may love us as children and honor us with heavenly honors.
Moses said, 'Sanctify to me every firstborn, every firstborn that opens the womb' (Exodus 13:2), meaning that these firstborns should be registered and dedicated as holy and indebted to God.

The law of God and the Father shows his eternal will by taking the spiritual likeness as a type, as Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, saying that if the Lord their God brings them into the land of the Canaanites, they should destroy every male that opens the womb and dedicate it to the Lord.
For all who are holy, wherever the image of the holy and firstborn Christ shines forth, are sanctified, set apart for God's service and conformed to the image of His Son.

Paul says that for those whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, and those whom he predestined, he also called, and those whom he called, he also justified, and those whom he justified, he also glorified (Romans 8:29-30).
The transcendent beauty, which is thought to be on the divine and supernatural substance, is the one that transforms us, conforming us to the image of Christ.

As the character is revealed in our souls, if we are partakers of the divine nature, having received the Spirit of the Father and the Son, we are transformed into the same image, from glory to glory, as from the Lord Spirit (2 Corinthians 3:18).

In deeds and in the power of virtue, the transformation and transfiguration in us take place, towards whatever is pleasing to God, and casting out all weakness of our mind, and transforming it into a firm and invincible phronema.
The law shows us the way to achieve this transformation, and it is through our participation in Christ that we can overcome the power of sin and be conformed to the image of God's Son.
